blocks.text: a) Determination of solubility from Ksp

With the formula of the compound and its Ksp value, the unknown molar solubility S is calculated and the concentrations of the ions determined. Table 9.6 relates Ksp values and the solubility of some sparingly soluble compounds.

blocks.caption: Solubility and solubility product (Table 9.6, as printed)
rows: 1.69 x 10^-4 (printed; 1.6 x 10^-8 in the text and Table 9.5)

blocks.text: Ca(OH)2 is sparingly soluble with Ksp = 6.5 x 10^-6; calculate its solubility. Let the solubility be S mol dm-3. The balanced equation Ca(OH)2 gives Ca2+ + 2OH- starts from 0 and 0 and reaches S and 2S at equilibrium; the concentration of OH- is double that of Ca2+, so Ksp = [Ca2+][OH-]^2 = S x (2S)^2 = 4S^3 = 6.5 x 10^-6. Then S^3 = 6.5 x 10^-6 / 4 = 1.625 x 10^-6, S = (1.625)^(1/3) x 10^-2 = 1.18 x 10^-2 mol dm-3. At equilibrium 1.18 x 10^-2 mol dm-3 of Ca2+ and 2 x 1.18 x 10^-2 = 2.36 x 10^-2 mol dm-3 of OH- are present; the individual ion concentrations have been found from the solubility product.

The presence of a common ion decreases the solubility of a slightly soluble ionic compound. In a saturated solution of the sparingly soluble salt PbCrO4, PbCrO4 gives Pb2+(aq) + CrO4 2-(aq); adding the soluble salt Na2CrO4 supplies the common ion CrO4 2-, which combines with Pb2+ to form more insoluble PbCrO4, so the equilibrium shifts to the left to keep Ksp constant.

The solubility product also predicts whether a salt will precipitate. The solubility product of CaSO4 is 2 x 10^-5. If 10^-2 mol dm-3 Ca2+ solution is added to 10^-2 mol dm-3 SO4 2- solution at 25 degrees C, each ion is diluted to [Ca2+] = [SO4 2-] = 10^-2 / 2 = 5.0 x 10^-3 mol dm-3, and the ionic product [Ca2+][SO4 2-] = 5.0 x 10^-3 x 5.0 x 10^-3 = 2.5 x 10^-5 mol2 dm-6, which is greater than Ksp, so CaSO4 precipitates.

blocks.prompt: Ksp of AgCl is 1.77 x 10^-10. Find the solubility of AgCl in 0.10 M NaCl, and predict whether CaSO4 precipitates when 10^-3 mol dm-3 Ca2+ and SO4 2- are mixed (Quick Check 9.5a, b).
blocks.explanation: In 0.10 M NaCl the chloride from the salt dominates: Ksp = [Ag+][Cl-] = S x 0.10, so S = 1.77 x 10^-10 / 0.10 = 1.8 x 10^-9 mol dm-3, far below the 1.3 x 10^-5 mol dm-3 in pure water (common ion effect). For CaSO4, mixing equal volumes halves each concentration to 5 x 10^-4, so the ionic product is 2.5 x 10^-7, less than Ksp = 2 x 10^-5: the solution is unsaturated and no precipitate forms.

items: Solubility from Ksp: for Ca(OH)2, Ksp = S(2S)^2 = 4S^3 = 6.5 x 10^-6 gives S = 1.18 x 10^-2 mol dm-3 and [OH-] = 2.36 x 10^-2 mol dm-3.
Common ion lowers solubility (Na2CrO4 added to saturated PbCrO4 shifts the equilibrium left); precipitation occurs only when the ionic product exceeds Ksp (CaSO4: 2.5 x 10^-5 greater than 2 x 10^-5).
